input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The wrapper now reuses one statistics dict across all calls and clears it on every call, so concurrent or nested invocations of the same decorated function share and overwrite each other's statistics.
- rationale: Trigger: two threads (or a recursive call) invoke the same decorated function while one call is in progress and reads its statistics. Mechanism: each new call runs stats.clear() on the shared dict and then the copy writes its attempt data into that same dict, so the in-flight call's statistics are reset or mixed with another call's. Previously each call got its own dict, so reads were isolated. Impact: callers reading attempt_number or other statistics from within a retried call get wrong values.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism: the wrapper reuses one shared statistics dict and calls stats.clear() on each call. Concurrent or nested calls therefore wipe and mix each other's attempt_number and start_time. This matches both the label's root cause and its failure path.
